text.p: - A Russian teacher who had not been paid for months died after failing to collect 300,000 roubles ($50) to buy medicine she needed for treatment.
- The Chechen leadership is split but not enough to start a civil war.

- Late Chechen leader Dzhokhar Dudayev was speaking on the phone to President Boris Yeltsin when he was killed by an explosion, says Dudayev's widow Alla Dudayeva in an interview to a Turkish newspaper.
- A second round will be needed to elect a new parliament in Chechnya.
- IMF presses the Russian government to go ahead with restructuring natural monopolies.
- U.S. President Bill Clinton says he has no reason not to believe official statements on President Yeltsin's health.
- Moscow, unlike Grozny, still thinks Chechnya is part of the Russian Federation.
- Russian politicians are working hard to find a way to stay in power in case President Yeltsin collapses.
- Aslan Maskhadov's victory in the presidential election in Chechnya will not embitter, lull or weaken the Kremlin.
- Moscow has to settle the problem of Azeri oil transport through Chechnya with the new leaders in Grozny before February 15 or face heavy fines from its foreign partners.
